hook.description: Cold open, no title card first: stop-motion husband (long-nosed, bespectacled, in a black suit, checking his phone) stands impatiently in a hallway/doorway and asks his wife 'Jane, how much longer?' while she is mid-makeup routine at her vanity in the bedroom beyond.
hook.why_it_works: Drops straight into a mid-argument line of dialogue with no preamble, instantly signaling a relatable domestic-couple scenario (partner waiting on partner) within the first 2.5 seconds, which is what stops the scroll.

setup.description: Jane replies defensively 'I said I was getting ready,' and the husband immediately counters with the specific, exaggerated callout 'That was 45 minutes ago,' establishing the classic 'getting ready takes forever' bit and the husband's growing impatience (reinforced visually by him repeatedly glancing at his phone).

conflict.description: Jane pushes back with a rhetorical trap: 'Do you want pretty or punctual?' turning the confrontation around on him and forcing an impossible choice, visually punctuated by an on-screen text overlay of 'PUNCTUAL?' as she says the line.

punchline.description: Jane delivers the flat, deadpan mic-drop line 'Pick a struggle,' closing the exchange with a dismissive, unbothered tone that undercuts the husband's frustration entirely.

ending.description: No further dialogue or action after the punchline; the scene holds briefly on the characters before cutting to a black title card.
ending.cta_or_text_overlay: Text card reads 'LOW BATTERY PEOPLE' with subtitle 'CREATED BY NIN.' — a branding/attribution end card rather than a narrative resolution or explicit call-to-action.
